thread.title: Apple's Stock Is Up Because Sales Are Looking Better Than Feared

title: Apple's Stock Is Up Because Sales Are Looking Better Than Feared
text:
Apple’s Stock Is Up Because Sales Are Looking Better Than Feared By Jan. 29, 2019 5:16 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Don Emmert/AFP/Getty Images Text size
Apple stock was up in after-hours trading after the iPhone maker reported slightly better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter earnings and offered a current-quarter forecast that wasn’t as terrible as some had feared.
The back story. Heading into today’s earnings, shares of Apple (ticker: AAPL) had fallen 30% since the company last reported results on Nov. 1. Concerns about the company’s sales in China and demand for its latest iPhone have mounted since then, highlighted by Apple’s rare warning earlier this month about lower-than-expected revenue for the December quarter. Analysts and investors obsess over iPhone results because the smartphone segment represents over 60% of Apple’s total revenue. Earlier today, a FaceTime bug further dampened the news cycle. Through it all, Apple has continued to tout the value of its massive installed base. Newsletter Sign-up
The numbers . Late Tuesday, Apple reported fiscal first-quarter earnings of $4.18 per share, a penny above Wall Street’s forecast for $4.17. Revenue of $84.31 billion also topped expectations for $83.97 billion, though Wall Street had already adjusted that number significantly downward after Apple’s warning on Jan. 3.
“While it was disappointing to miss our revenue guidance, we manage Apple for the long term, and this quarter’s results demonstrate that the underlying strength of our business runs deep and wide,” Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook said in a statement announcing the results.
The key number from today’s report was Apple’s fiscal second-quarter sales guidance of $55 billion to $59 billion. That wasn’t far off from Wall Street’s own $59 billion forecast. Given Apple’s recent trouble that counted as good news.
Apple no longer breaks out iPhone unit shipments , but sales of the smartphone slipped 15% to $51.98 billion year-over-year. The company’s services division—home to products like iCloud, iTunes, and Apple Music—jumped 19% in the same period, to a record $10.9 billion. The company said its active installed base of devices reached an all-time high of 1.4 billion.
Looking ahead. Apple shares are up 3.7% in after-hours trading. The company is currently holding a conference call with analysts. Analysts will be looking for more details about the company’s services strategy , as well as an update on business in China and about the performance of the new iPhone XR model.
